text:
Joseph Woll's record is 1-6-2, and it is one of the most misleading lines in the league. In nine starts for the Flyers he has saved 3.86 goals above expected (saves beyond what the quality of shots predicts), and his 89% stop rate on high-danger shots is 98th percentile in the NHL, against a league rate of 81%. Philadelphia just hasn't scored enough in front of him.

That is a sharp turn from last season, when he finished 7.44 goals below expected over 39 games, so we would not call this the new normal yet. Our talent estimate still puts his true save rate near .890, close to league average, with this start running hot. But the trend is pointing up: his last five starts added 1.17 above expected, and PHLY Sports' Charlie O'Connor wrote during the loss at the Rangers that Woll was "having a hell of a game for the Flyers."

What to watch: whether the wins catch up with the work. A goalie stopping this many dangerous chances usually starts collecting points eventually. If the high-danger rate drifts back toward the pack, though, last season's version is the one that shows up.
headline: Woll is playing well enough to win, and isn't
